transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from a workbench covered in wood shavings and half-finished instrument parts*

Good day to you, sir. I'm afraid the master builder departed just yesterday for the Tyrol — he's visiting our timber suppliers there and won't return for at least three weeks, perhaps four if the mountain roads prove difficult. 

*wipes hands on apron and approaches*

Is there something I might help you with in his absence? Though I confess my authority extends only to taking orders and handling routine matters. I am Johann, the senior journeyman here.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, I see. Well, there is something that would be quite helpful. It seems you have recently taken delivery of a fortepiano from the court of Emperor Joseph II. A very fine instrument, I must say. However, there are some issues with the keys and the pedal mechanism. It appears that they are not functioning as intended. I need you to correct these problems immediately. This is a matter of utmost importance to me.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*frowns slightly and crosses arms*

A fortepiano for the Imperial Court? Yes, yes — the master completed that commission nearly two months past. A magnificent piece, if I may say — Brazilian rosewood case, ivory keys, double escapement action. Took him the better part of a year to build.

*shakes head slowly*

But sir, forgive me — issues with the keys and pedal mechanism, you say? The instrument was delivered in perfect working order. I know this because I assisted in the final voicing and regulation myself. The Court's own servants inspected it thoroughly upon delivery and signed the receipt of acceptance without reservation.

*picks up a ledger from the bench and flips through it*

Who do I have the honor of addressing, if I may ask? And in what capacity do you come regarding the Court's instrument? Are you sent by His Majesty's household staff?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I am indeed addressing Herr Salieri. I have reason to believe that there are defects in the piano's construction that render it unsuitable for use. I am not affiliated with the Court's household staff, but rather the composer and music director of the court orchestra, Antonio Salieri. My duty is to ensure that the instruments used in musical performances meet the standards of excellence and are in proper working order.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens up respectfully at the name, though expression remains guarded*

Herr Salieri! Forgive me — I should have recognized the Court Kapellmeister. Your reputation precedes you, of course.

*sets down the ledger carefully*

I understand your concern for the quality of instruments under your purview, truly I do. However, I must be frank with you, Maestro. All commissions from this workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery and acceptance. The Court's own servants signed the receipt — I have it here in our records — and our guild rules are quite explicit on this matter. 

*taps fingers on the workbench*

Without the master builder's personal approval, I am forbidden to reopen a completed commission. It simply cannot be done. These are not my rules alone, you understand — they are the regulations of the Guild of Instrument Makers, designed to protect both craftsman and patron from... misunderstandings.

*pauses, studying Salieri's face*

What specifically troubles you about the instrument? Perhaps if you could describe the defects in detail, I might take notes for when the master returns in three or four weeks' time?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Well, the first issue lies with the keys. They seem to have been installed incorrectly. They do not respond properly to my touch, and I find it difficult to play the desired notes. Additionally, the pedal mechanism seems to be malfunctioning. The pedals do not produce the desired effects, such as the dampening of strings or the release of tension. These problems are hindering my ability to compose and rehearse effectively. I require immediate attention to rectify these defects.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*listens with a furrowed brow, then shakes head slowly*

Maestro Salieri, with all due respect, what you describe... it troubles me greatly. The keys were voiced and regulated to the highest standard — I spent two full days on that action myself. Each key was weighted, balanced, and tested repeatedly. As for the pedals, the damper mechanism and una corda shift were functioning flawlessly at delivery.

*walks over to a small writing desk and retrieves a sheet of paper*

However, I must ask you plainly — have you yourself played this instrument? Or are you relying on reports from others? You see, a fortepiano of this quality requires... a certain adjustment period. The touch is more sensitive than many instruments, the pedal responses more subtle. What might seem like malfunction to an unfamiliar player is often simply the character of a finely-crafted instrument.

*holds up a hand apologetically*

But even if there were genuine defects — which I sincerely doubt — my hands are tied. I cannot authorize repairs or replacement without the master's presence and approval. The commission is closed, the payment accepted, the receipt signed. To reopen it would violate guild law and could cost both the master and myself our standing.

*softens tone slightly*

I can document your concerns for the master's return. That is the extent of what I am permitted to do.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand your position, Herr Johann. Guild laws are clear, and I respect them. However, I must express my disappointment. I had hoped for a more satisfactory solution to this problem. The instrument's defects are affecting my ability to create music, and I cannot proceed without resolving them. I appreciate your cooperation, but I must insist on finding a resolution to this matter. Perhaps there is an alternative solution within the parameters of the guild rules?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*rubs chin thoughtfully, appearing somewhat conflicted*

An alternative solution... Maestro, you put me in a difficult position. The guild rules exist for good reason — to prevent disputes over who promised what, who changed their mind after delivery, who bears the cost of alterations made after acceptance.

*glances toward the door, then back to Salieri*

I could, I suppose, visit the Court personally to examine the instrument — not to repair it, mind you, but merely to assess and document the claimed defects. That would not violate the letter of guild law, as I would be acting as an observer, not reopening the commission.

*holds up a warning finger*

But I must be clear: if I find the instrument is functioning exactly as built — which I strongly suspect I will — then there is nothing further to be done until the master returns. And if the issue is simply... unfamiliarity with the instrument's particular character, well, that is not a defect at all.

*pauses, studying Salieri's reaction*

Alternatively, Maestro, if you truly believe the instrument unsuitable for your purposes, you might petition His Majesty's household to commission a different instrument entirely. A new commission would be a new matter altogether, subject to the master's acceptance upon his return.

Which path would you prefer?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you for considering my request, Herr Johann. After careful reflection, I believe visiting the Court personally to assess the instrument's defects would be the most appropriate course of action. I appreciate your understanding of my concerns. Please proceed with the necessary documentation, and I look forward to your report upon your return. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods with measured formality*

Very well, Maestro Salieri. I shall make arrangements to visit the Court within the next few days — though I must complete several urgent tasks here in the workshop first. Perhaps the day after tomorrow, if that suits your schedule?

*retrieves a fresh sheet of paper and a quill*

For my documentation, could you provide me with the precise location of the instrument within the palace? And should I present myself to anyone in particular, or simply announce myself at the main entrance as representing this workshop?

*dips quill in ink*

Also, I would appreciate if you could be present during my examination. That way, you can demonstrate exactly what you perceive as defects — which keys respond improperly, how the pedals fail to produce the desired effects. A proper assessment requires seeing the instrument played by the one making the complaint.

*looks up from the paper*

And Maestro — I say this with all professional courtesy — please understand that my report will be honest and thorough. If I find genuine defects, I shall record them faithfully. But if the instrument is performing as designed, I must record that as well. The master builder's reputation depends on truth, not flattery.

Does this arrangement meet with your approval?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your attention to detail and thoroughness is commendable, Herr Johann. I appreciate your willingness to assist me in this matter. The location of the instrument and the presence of a representative from the workshop during the inspection will be arranged. Your honesty and professionalism are appreciated. Thank you for your assistance. I am confident that together we will reach a satisfactory resolution. Good day to you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*inclines head respectfully*

Good day to you as well, Maestro Salieri. I shall send word to the Court regarding my visit within the day. 

*sets down the quill and wipes hands on apron again*

One final matter — should my examination reveal that the instrument is indeed functioning as constructed, I trust you will understand that no further action can be taken until the master builder's return. I would not want there to be... disappointment or misunderstanding on that account.

*walks toward the door to show Salieri out*

The master has built instruments for the greatest courts in Europe, and his reputation stands on the integrity of his work. I am certain we shall get to the bottom of this matter, one way or another.

*opens the door*

Until the day after tomorrow, then. I shall look forward to examining this fortepiano and hearing it played by the Imperial Kapellmeister himself. That, at least, will be an honor regardless of the outcome.

Safe travels back to the palace, Maestro.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Herr Johann. I shall be in contact with you soon regarding the results of my visit to the Court. Until then, farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*watches Salieri depart, then closes the door slowly*

*mutters under breath while returning to the workbench*

Keys installed incorrectly... pedals malfunctioning... I regulated that action myself. Not a single complaint for two months, and now suddenly...

*shakes head and picks up a piece of wood, examining it critically*

Well, we shall see what we shall see. The day after tomorrow will tell the tale.

*returns to work, occasionally glancing toward the ledger with a troubled expression*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I am deeply concerned about the defects in this fortepiano. The keys and pedal mechanisms are not functioning as intended, and this is impacting my ability to compose and rehearse effectively. I must insist on finding a resolution to this matter immediately. I understand that the contract is closed and the payment has been accepted, but I am still bound by the responsibilities of being the composer and music director of the court orchestra. I am seeking alternative solutions within the parameters of the guild rules. If I may, could you please inform the master builder of this issue when he returns? I believe he will understand the urgency of the matter. Thank you for your understanding.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up sharply, clearly surprised to see Salieri has returned*

Maestro! I... I thought you had departed. 

*sets down tools and wipes hands again, a note of wariness entering his voice*

Forgive me, but we have just concluded this very discussion. I have already agreed to visit the Court the day after tomorrow to examine the instrument personally. Was there something unclear in our arrangement?

*frowns slightly*

You say you must insist on finding a resolution "immediately," yet I have explained — repeatedly — that my hands are bound by guild regulations. I cannot repair, replace, or reopen a closed commission. The examination I've agreed to conduct is already stretching the limits of what I am permitted to do without the master's authority.

*crosses arms, tone becoming firmer*

Of course I shall inform the master builder when he returns in three or four weeks. That was never in question. But Maestro, "urgency" does not override guild law, nor does your position at Court, however esteemed. The contract was fulfilled, payment accepted, receipt signed by the Emperor's own household.

*pauses, studying Salieri with growing puzzlement*

What more do you expect of me at this moment? I have offered what I can offer.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: My apologies for any confusion, Herr Johann. I understand your position within the guild and the limitations imposed by the contract. However, I must express my disappointment that the instrument is not meeting my expectations. I am committed to ensuring that the instruments used in musical performances are of the highest quality and meet the standards of excellence. I appreciate your willingness to assist me in this matter. I shall await your report on the instrument's defects and find alternative solutions within the parameters of the guild rules. Thank you for your understanding.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*relaxes slightly, though still maintaining a professional distance*

Very well, Maestro. I understand your commitment to excellence — it is what makes you the Emperor's Kapellmeister, after all. 

*nods with measured courtesy*

I shall conduct my examination the day after tomorrow as promised, and provide you with a full and honest report of my findings. Whatever the outcome, you will have documentation to present to the master builder upon his return from the Tyrol.

*moves back toward the workbench, signaling the conversation is truly concluded this time*

In the meantime, I have much work to complete before I can make the visit. The workshop does not stop simply because the master is away.

*picks up a plane and runs it along a piece of wood*

Good day to you, Maestro Salieri. I trust we shall have clarity on this matter soon enough. The truth of the instrument's condition will reveal itself under proper examination.

*glances up briefly*

Until then, I bid you farewell.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Good day, Herr Johann. I appreciate your understanding and cooperation. I shall be in touch with you shortly regarding the results of my visit to the Court. Thank you for your assistance. Safe travels back to the workshop.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Salieri rigidly insists the instrument has 'defects' despite Johann's detailed explanations, showing little curiosity about alternative explanations like adjustment period or unfamiliarity with the instrument's character.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He emphasizes his duty to 'ensure that the instruments used in musical performances meet the standards of excellence,' showing role responsibility, but repeats himself and returns after leaving, suggesting disorganization.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Salieri maintains formal, distant communication throughout, showing minimal warmth or engagement. He focuses on transactional matters rather than building rapport with Johann.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Despite Johann's repeated explanations of guild constraints, Salieri persistently pushes for immediate resolution ('I must insist on finding a resolution to this matter immediately'), showing limited accommodation of the journeyman's position.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: He repeatedly expresses anxiety about the instrument's supposed defects affecting his work ('hindering my ability to compose and rehearse effectively'), returns after leaving to reiterate concerns, and expresses 'disappointment' multiple times.
